headline: Zoning Board approves variances for 16 Gibson Road, 25 Draper Street, 365 Princeton Boulevard, and 235 Ludlam Street; continues 80 Seventh Avenue to August 10
summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals held public hearings on five variance petitions. It approved variances at 16 Gibson Road, 25 Draper Street, 365 Princeton Boulevard, and 235 Ludlam Street (with a dumpster screening condition), and continued the petition for 80 Seventh Avenue to the August 10 meeting. The board also approved minutes from June 22, 2026.
decisions: Approved the variance for James Tessier to convert an existing garage into living space at 16 Gibson Road, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Patrick and Renee Welch to construct an addition at 25 Draper Street, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Salath Tek to construct a roof over an existing porch at 365 Princeton Boulevard, 5-0.
Continued the variance petition for Michael Brown to construct a new single-family home at 80 Seventh Avenue to the August 10 meeting, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Johnny Arteaga for a second curb cut and additional paving at 235 Ludlam Street, with a condition to screen the dumpster, 5-0.
Approved the minutes of 6/22/2026, 3-0, with two members abstaining.

plain_text:
Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals Minutes 
7/13/2026 at 6:30 P.M.  
 
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, contact the Division of 
Development Services, 375 Merrimack Street, Lowell, MA or refer to video recordings available online 
at www.LTC.org. 
 
Members Present: Chairman Pech,  Vice Chair Callahan , Member Briere, Member Procope, Member 
Hovey, Member Shanahan 
 
Members Absent: Member McCarthy 
 
Others Present: Mary Brundage, Associate Planner 
 
The following represents the actions taken by the Zoning Board of Appeals at the 7/13/2026 meeting. This 
meeting was held in the  City Council Chamber . Attendees had the ability to participate via Zoom as 
permitted by Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, signed into law on March 28, 2025. 
 
Chairman Pech called the meeting to order at 6:30 PM. 
I. Continued Business 
 
 
II. New Business 
ZBA-2026-25  
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: James Tessier  
Property Located at: 16 Gibson Road, 01851  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by James Tessier to convert an existing garage into living space at 16 Gibson 
Road. The subject property is located in the Suburban Sing le Family (SSF) zoning district. The proposal 
requires Variance approval per Section 5.1 for relief for maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and any other 
relief required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance.    
 
On Behalf: 
James Tessier 
J. Tessier stated that the request is to convert garage into living space for entertaining. The addition will 
include a bathroom and kitchenette that will be mainly used with the pool. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None
Discussion: 
T. Hovey stated it was a  great plan. He pointed out that the comment memo mentions the amount of 
hardscape and the potential to add trees. He did not feel the need to add trees. The petition was for the 
living space, not the patio. He stated was in favor of the petition. 
 
M. Briere stated that the relief request is modest and is in support. 
 
G. Procope stated that he is in favor of project and that it was not a detriment. 
 
S. Callahan stated he had no objections. He asked about the amount of hardscape. J. Tessier responded 
that the current deck will be demolished and the patio will put in its place. J. Tessier further explained 
that the driveway going to the garage will be fenced off. S. Callahan noted that the plan has a significa nt 
number of trees to be planted. 
 
D. Shanahan stated that the request is reasonable and is in favor. 
 
V. Pech agreed with the other members and stated that was a nice addition. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to approve the variance S. Callahan seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-26   
Petition Type: Variance   
Applicant: Patrick and Renee Welch  
Property Located at: 25 Draper Street, 01852  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1   
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Patrick and Renee Welch to construct an addition. The subject property is 
located in the Suburban Single Family (SSF) zoning district. The proposal requires Variance approval per 
Section 5.1 for relief for minimum side yard setbacks and any other relief required under the Lowell 
Zoning Ordinance.    
 
On Behalf: 
Patrick and Renee Welch 
P. Welch stated that they moved from a bigger house in Dracut. The proposed addition would be 12’ x 25’ 
with a bathroom. He stated that they needed a bit more living space for family gatherings. The addition is 
just shy of 16 inches required for the right-hand side setback. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion:
M. Briere asked if the applicant had seen the proposed comment from the water department. P. Welch 
stated that they sent the plan from their plumber with the water connections to DPD. M. Brundage 
confirmed it was received and forwarded to the board. M. Briere stated he was in favor of this plan. 
 
G. Procope stated that it was a minimal ask and keeping family together is part of zoning. 
 
S. Callahan agreed that the request was minimal. He mentioned the possibility for free shade trees. M. 
Brundage stated that she would look into it. 
 
D. Shanahan stated that the request is minimal and will be voting in favor. 
 
T. Hovey did not have any further questions. 
 
V. Pech agreed that the request is minimal and would add value to the home. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to approve the variance. T. Hovey seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-27  
Petition Type: Variance   
Applicant: Salath Tek  
Property Located at: 365 Princeton Boulevard, 01851  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1   
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Salath Tek to construct a roof to an existing porch at 365 Princeton Blvd. 
The subject property is located in the Traditional Single-Family (TSF) zoning district. The proposal 
requires Variance approval per Section 5.1 for relief from the maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR) 
requirement, and for any other relief required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Salath Tek stated that he is requesting to put a roof over his existing deck. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
G. Procope stated that is a  minimal ask. He mentioned that it is a b eautiful property and that it m akes 
sense to add the roof. 
 
S. Callahan asked if the roof was to be over hanged and not enclosed. S. Tek confirmed that it would just 
overhang. S. Callahan stated it was a reasonable request as long it was a canopy style roof. 
 
D. Shanahan had no issues. 
 
T. Hovey had no further comment.
M. Briere had did not have any further questions. 
 
V. Pech had no concerns and agreed that it was a minimal ask. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to approve the variance. T. Hovey seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0).  
 
ZBA-2026-28  
Petition Type: Variance   
Applicant: Michael Brown  
Property Located at: 80 Seventh Avenue, 01854  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1   
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Michael Brown to construct a new single-family home at 80 Seventh Ave. The 
subject property is located in the Traditional Neighborhoo d Single Family (TSF) zoning district. The 
proposal requires a Variance per Section 5.1 for relief from the minimum frontage requirement, maximum 
front yard setback and any other relief required under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
 
Speaking in Favor: 
 
Discussion: 
V. Pech noted that the applicant requested a continuance to the next meeting. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to continue to August 10 Meeting . M. Briere seconded.  The vote was unanimous 
(5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-29  
Petition Type: Variance   
Applicant: Johnny Arteaga  
Property Located at: 235 Ludlam Street, 01850  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 6.1   
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Johnny Arteaga for a second curb cut and additional paving at 235 Ludlam 
Street. The subject property is located in the Traditional M ulti-Family (TMF) zoning district. The proposal 
requires a Variance per Section 6.1 for relief from the maximum curbcut and any other relief required 
under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance.    
 
On Behalf: 
Johnny Arteaga 
J. Arteaga stated that is requesting a variance for a second curb cut to provide access to designated waste 
management area for this six -unit residential building. The purpose of proposal is to have a designated 
area that can accommodate either a traditional dumpster or a wheeled dumpster. This would eliminate
the need for 12 individual containers along the street, reducing clutter, improving car space and be more 
efficient. He stated that the request will overall improve the property and the neighborhood.  He noted 
that there was no opposition on this proposal from the city departments. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
Sirohi Aditya, 83-85 Aiken Avenue 
S. Aditya expressed concerns about the space for dump truck access. He was also concerned about the 
capacity of dumpster and potential sanitary and o dor issues. He also mentioned concerns about snow 
removal and the impact on on-street parking. He mentioned that a tree was removed and requested that 
a tree be added to the landscape plan. 
 
J. Arteaga responded that he previously handled trash collection at that property and stated that the six 
or more barrels will take up more space and that the trash will not be picked up if the cars are near it, 
creating more issues. This proposal will eliminate the accumulation of more trash and sanitation concerns. 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
S. Callahan stated that he understood the abutter’s concerns but commended the applican t for coming 
up with a solution for trash removal. He asked if the  designated area would be just for t rash and would 
there still be bins  out for recycling. J. Arteaga responded that he might look into adding a recycling 
dumpster. J. Arteaga stated that they will be using a wheeled dumpster so that the truck will not have to 
go into the area. He mentioned that he will be gating the whole perimeter of the property with a six-foot 
fence. S. Callahan confirmed if the curb cut on Ludlam Street is 25 feet. J. Arteaga confirmed that the curb 
cut would be three feet from the house and retaining wall.  S. Callahan stated that the applicant is doing 
what he can in eliminating abutter concerns. The alternative would 12 bins on the street. He stated he is 
in favor of the proposal. 
 
D. Shanahan stated that waste removal is challenging. He asked if the applicant is currently using a private 
removal company. J. Arteaga responded that he is since it is required for a commercial property over four 
units. D. Shanahan that it is not a continuous curb cut of 35 feet and is in favor of the proposal. 
 
T. Hovey asked if there could be condition to put fencing around the back and two sides of the dumpster. 
J. Arteaga was agreeable to that. 
 
M. Briere stated that the narrative is excellent and that the existing problems are being mitigated by this 
plan is a good resolution. He stated he is in favor of this plan. 
 
G. Procope stated that the intent is to try to improve the area and ensure trash is being picked up. Once 
implemented, hopefully the abutter will see as an improvement. 
 
V. Pech stated that the steps have been taken to address access, screening and proximity with the 
sanitation issues with the neighbors . V. Pech asked if the applicant was okay with the condition to the 
screen the dumpster on three sides. J. Arteaga state that he was okay with it.
S. Callahan mentioned the possibility of screening the top of the dumpster. J. Arteaga was not opposed to 
it. Ultimately, the top screening could become problematic in opening the dumpster. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to approve with the following condition. T. Hovey seconded. The vote was 
unanimous (5-0). 
1.  The applicant shall screen the dumpster on all sides with the exception of the side for access to 
the dumpster. 
III. Other Business 
Minutes for Approval:   
6/22/2026 
 
G. Procope motioned to approve the minutes. T. Hovey seconded . The vote was unanimous (3-0) with S. 
Callahan and D. Shanahan abstaining. 
 
Adjournment  
G. Procope motioned to adjourn. S. Callahan seconded. Motion passed unanimously (5-0). 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:26 PM
